model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity on adjusted earnings (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: Preferred stock (Series D/F/G/H/I/J/K outstanding after 2025-26 redemptions), carrying value
equity_bridge.note: XBRL PreferredStockValue at 2026-06-30 (down from 9,191 at Dec-24 after $2,458M redeemed in 2025 and $2,055M in H1-2026). Senior to common; deducted at par instead of charging the ~$300M/yr preferred dividend to the flows.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case FY2027-FY2031 average revenue growth (8.0, 7.0, 6.5, 6.0, 5.5); equity CAGR rejected as the anchor because it is driven by AOCI marks, the FY2020 TD Ameritrade share issuance and preferred redemptions rather than earnings power
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR -2.5% vs revenue 15.4% and EPS 17.0% - divergence >30%. Causes: (1) FY2020 equity of 56,060 was inflated by the all-stock TD Ameritrade acquisition, (2) AOCI swung from positive to -14.8B in 2022-24 as rates rose, (3) $4.5B of preferred redeemed 2025-26 and >100% payout via buybacks. The 5-yr revenue/EPS CAGRs are themselves flattered by the TDA acquisition (closed 6 Oct 2020, so the FY2020 base holds only one quarter of TDA); the 3-yr figures (4.8% revenue, 9.9% EPS) span the 2023 cash-sorting trough and are the cleaner organic read.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are computed on NET INCOME (the FCFE proxy: FY2025 8,852 vs FY2022 7,183 vs FY2020 3,299), not on the CSV's reported FCF, which is client-cash noise for a bank/broker (FY2023 18,783, FY2024 2,050, FY2025 8,709). Revenue: FY2025 23,921 / FY2022 20,762 / FY2020 11,691. EPS (CSV): 4.67 / 3.52 / 2.13. Equity: 49,425 / 36,608 / 56,060. All FY-end December.

scenario_narratives.base: Schwab's value turns on three things: (1) organic asset gathering - core NNA of ~5.5-6% a year on $13.1T of client assets, the #1 RIA custody franchise and 48M accounts, which compounds asset-management fees and the sweep-cash base; (2) net interest revenue (~half of revenue), where the post-2023 balance-sheet normalisation is largely done - supplemental funding is down to $0.5B of FHLB advances - so the base case holds the 52.5% adjusted pretax margin through FY2028 and then gives back 150bps to 51% as Fed easing narrows new-money spreads; (3) capital return - with integration finished and AOCI recovering, ~85-90% of adjusted earnings is distributed via buybacks and a $1.28 dividend. Revenue grows 8% in FY2027 fading to 3.5% by FY2036. Valued as FCFE at a 10% cost of equity with the $6.2B preferred deducted, this lands close to the current price: the market is already paying for the normalisation.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Q2-2026 run-rate proves to be a floor: record NNA (Q2 +49% YoY, June the largest month ever) sustains 6-7% organic growth, BDA balances keep migrating onto Schwab's balance sheet and legacy low-yield securities reprice into record loan originations, so the adjusted pretax margin climbs to 55% - the operating leverage a fully integrated TDA platform should deliver. AOCI pull-to-par releases capital, so retention falls to 0.6x growth and payout runs near 100%. Revenue grows 11% in FY2027, 4% by FY2036, terminal growth 3.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: 2023 repeats in milder form: short rates stay elevated relative to sweep yields, clients sort cash into money-market funds, and Schwab re-levers onto FHLB and brokered funding while a market drawdown cuts fee and trading revenue. FY2027 revenue falls 6%, the adjusted pretax margin drops to 43% (FY2024 was ~41.5%), buybacks pause to rebuild leverage capital, and the franchise then grows only 3-4.5% with the margin recovering to 46%. Exit at 12x FCFE. No solvency element - the RIA and retail franchise is intact; this is an earnings reset and a de-rating, not a credit event.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Schwab is a savings-and-loan holding company whose economics are those of a deposit-funded bank wrapped around a fee-earning brokerage and custody franchise, so it is valued as free cash flow to equity - adjusted net income (before non-cash amortization of TD Ameritrade intangibles) less the capital retained to grow the balance sheet at its leverage target - capitalised at a 10% USD cost of equity. Deposits, FHLB advances and senior notes are operating funding already charged inside net interest revenue, so net debt is zero and only the $6.2B preferred is deducted ahead of common. FY0 is the FY2026 run-rate; the three cases differ on whether the post-2023 net-interest-margin recovery holds, extends or reverses through another cash-sorting episode.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cash sorting: if short-term rates stay elevated versus sweep yields, client cash migrates to money-market funds and Schwab re-levers onto costlier FHLB/brokered funding, compressing net interest revenue (~half of revenue) - the bear case's FY2027 -6% revenue and 43% margin
Rate path: Fed easing narrows the spread on new asset purchases even as funding costs fall; the base case already gives back 150bps of margin from FY2029
Equity-market levels drive asset-management fees and trading activity (~40% of revenue combined); a 20% drawdown would cut both with little cost offset

AOCI (-$10.6B) depresses tangible common equity to ~$14/share; if regulation (Basel III endgame for Category III firms) forces AOCI into regulatory capital before pull-to-par completes, buybacks slow and retention rises

The model excludes ~$540M/yr of acquired-intangible amortization from the flows as non-cash; that is correct for FCFE but means the valuation sits on adjusted, not GAAP, earnings (GAAP EPS ~$0.25/yr lower)

The share count is held flat and buybacks are treated as the distribution channel; per-share value is therefore insensitive to repurchase pace but sensitive to the 10% cost of equity and the 0.8x retention ratio (see sensitivity grid)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 83.96-114.53
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0000316709): FY2025 10-K filed 2026-02-25 and Q2-2026 10-Q filed 2026-08-07 for revenues, net interest revenue, noninterest expense, pretax income, tax, intangible amortization, SBC, capex, buybacks, dividends (common and preferred), preferred stock, goodwill, intangibles, AOCI, deposits, borrowings and share counts; SCHW_Metrics.csv (XBRL-derived) for the FY2007-Q2 2026 history
data_sources.qualitative: SCHW_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): Q1/Q2-2026 results, core NNA and account growth, balance-sheet normalisation and BDA transfers, cash-sorting and rate-sensitivity risks, TD Ameritrade integration completion, consensus EPS and price targets

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY0 = FY2026E total net revenues (net interest revenue + asset management/administration fees + trading + bank deposit account fees + other). Built from H1-2026 actuals of 13,554 (Q1 6,482, Q2 7,072; XBRL Revenues tag) plus an H2 of ~14,650 (Q3 ~7,250, Q4 ~7,400: Q2 exit run-rate grown by continued core NNA of ~5.8% annualised and further supplemental-funding paydown). 28,200 is +17.9% on FY2025's 23,921, consistent with the +16%/+21% YoY prints of Q1/Q2 and with FY2026 consensus EPS of ~$6.46 (adjusted). Schwab issues no formal revenue guidance; FY0 is a run-rate estimate, not a company number.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 10-Q cover-page common shares outstanding 1,729,335,714 (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding as of 2026-07-31, filed 2026-08-07, after H1-2026 buybacks of $3,377M) plus ~4.0M dilutive awards (Q2-2026 diluted 1,739M less basic 1,735M weighted average). TD Bank's former nonvoting stake was sold and converted in 2025, so there is one common class. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed inside compensation, and buybacks ($7,346M FY2025, $3,377M H1-2026) are the FCFE distribution channel, not a separately modelled count reduction.
inputs.net_debt_note: Bank convention (house precedent NAB.AX, HBAN, NTRS, GL): bank deposits ($249.7B at 2026-06-30), FHLB advances ($0.5B), other short-term borrowings ($13.9B) and senior notes (~$23.0B carrying amount) are operating funding of a savings-and-loan holding company, serviced inside net interest revenue. FCFE is post-interest, so net debt is held at 0 and the flows are capitalised at the cost of equity. Cash ($40.6B) is likewise operating liquidity of the bank and broker-dealer (segregated/regulatory), not surplus. The only claim senior to common deducted is the $6,213M of preferred stock (equity_bridge).
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is the FY2026E FCFE proxy: adjusted net income 11,326 (adjusted pretax 14,805 = 52.5% of 28,200, i.e. before the ~550/yr amortization of acquired TD Ameritrade intangibles, taxed at 23.5%) less 1,354 of capital retention at 0.8 x a normalised 6% balance-sheet growth (FY2026's +17.9% revenue growth is mostly NIM recovery as supplemental funding is repaid, which consumes no capital). reported_fcf is the CSV's FY2025 OCF-less-capex (8,709); it is deposit/brokerage-flow noise for this business (FY2024 2,050; FY2023 18,783; H1-2024 -5,839) and is recorded for auditability only. The owner-FCF identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income deliberately does NOT hold on this route.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL ShareBasedCompensation: FY2025 $317M (1.33% of revenue), H1-2026 $230M (1.70%, Q1 seasonally heavy). No separate net-share-settlement withholding figure is tagged; it is treated as part of buyback cash. SBC sits inside compensation expense, so the pretax margin is post-SBC; sbc_pct_path is carried so the engine's house/street band is computed.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: net interest revenue IS the business (~$11.75B FY2025, 49% of net revenues). Nothing is added back as net cash, so there is no double count.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock $7,346M + common dividends $1,958M = $9,304M returned vs $8,417M net income to common (111% payout, helped by AOCI pull-to-par and the TD stake sale overhang clearing). H1-2026: buybacks $3,377M + common dividends $1,123M = $4,500M (89% of $5,078M) while ALSO redeeming $2,055M of preferred. Quarterly dividend raised to $0.32 ($1.28 annualised, 1.3% yield).
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the FY2026 run-rate estimate (fiscal year closes 31 Dec 2026; H1 reported, Q3 due 2026-10-15), so Y1 = FY2027. Last fully reported year is FY2025.

balance_sheet_anchors.note: All from SEC XBRL, Q2-2026 10-Q. AOCI has recovered from -14,848 (Dec-24) to -10,575 as the legacy AFS/HTM book amortises to par; that pull-to-par is capital that becomes distributable over the next several years and is NOT separately credited in the base case (it is part of the bull case's lower retention).

inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 10.0% in USD: 10-yr UST ~4.25%, equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~1.15. Above NTRS's 9.75% because SCHW's net interest revenue (~half of revenue) carries the cash-sorting/deposit-duration risk that produced the 2023 episode, and the AOCI hole still sits against tangible book. One rate across all three scenarios, so risk is charged once, through the scenario paths and weights. Labelled 'wacc' only because that is the engine field; no debt is in the capital structure being discounted.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (branches, offices) are expensed inside occupancy/equipment expense and therefore inside the pretax margin; no lease liability is added to net debt (treatment A, applied once).
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; net income is fully attributable to the parent.
inputs.engine_mapping: The component engine is driven as a bank P&L: 'EBITDA margin' = ADJUSTED pretax margin + D&A % + SBC %, so that EBITDA - SBC - D&A = adjusted pretax income (GAAP pretax + amortization of acquired intangibles: FY2025 11,459 + 512 = 11,971 = 50.0% of revenue; H1-2026 6,857 + 274 = 7,131 = 52.6%; Q2-2026 53.9%). Acquired-intangible amortization (~$540M/yr, TD Ameritrade customer relationships, $7.3B left) is non-cash and requires no reinvestment, so excluding it is what an FCFE basis requires; it is not capitalised beyond its run-off because terminal flows are built on the same adjusted margin only as a matter of definition - see key risks. cash_tax_rate 23.5% (GAAP effective FY2025 22.8%, H1-2026 23.0%) applies to adjusted pretax. D&A and core capex share a 2.3% core (FY2025 capex 548 = 2.3% of revenue; depreciation runs above capex post-integration, so D&A=capex is conservative), and the EXCESS of capex_pct over da_pct is the capital retained to grow the balance sheet at Schwab's ~7% Tier-1 leverage operating target: retention = k x revenue growth, k = 0.8 base / 0.6 bull / 1.2 bear (TCE ex-AOCI / revenue ~1.24x, so k = 1.2 is one-for-one capital growth; 0.8 reflects that ~half of revenue is asset-based fees and trading that consume little capital). Working-capital capture 0. Result: FCFE = adjusted net income - retained capital, at the cost of equity; the $6.2B preferred is deducted at par in the bridge rather than its ~$300M/yr dividend charged to the flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine route - the routing table's bank row implemented as the house precedent for HBAN, NTRS, NAB.AX and GL: net_debt = 0, preferred deducted in equity_bridge, retention tied to growth. Residual income / BVPS on tangible book rejected as the primary model because SCHW's tangible common equity ($24.4B, $14/share) is depressed by a -$10.6B AOCI mark and by $19.6B of TD Ameritrade goodwill/intangibles, and the company distributes ~90-110% of earnings, so book is not the value driver; an owner-FCF DCF was rejected because OCF swings with client cash and brokerage payables (FY2023 +19.6B, FY2024 +2.7B, H1-2024 -5.6B). First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry, no prior DCF). FY0 ANCHOR: FY2026E revenue 28,200, adjusted pretax margin 52.5%, adjusted net income 11,326, less ~300 preferred dividends = ~$6.36 adjusted EPS on 1,733.3M diluted shares (15.5x at the current price; consensus FY2026 adjusted $6.46, FY2027 $7.83). DATA NOTES: CSV EPS FY2025 4.67 vs XBRL diluted 4.65; CSV Revenue rows are total net revenues (checked Q2-2026 7,072 = XBRL Revenues = earnings release) so the ASC-606 subset trap seen on NTRS/HBAN does NOT apply here; D&A is not XBRL-tagged after FY2023 (kpis ebitda_da stops at 804 in FY2023).

bear.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied adjusted pretax margin [43.0, 44.0, 45.0, 45.5, 46.0, 46.0, ...]: a renewed cash-sorting episode (short rates stay high relative to sweep yields) forces Schwab back onto FHLB/brokered funding, NIM compresses and a market drawdown cuts fees and trading; FY2027 revenue falls 6% against a sticky cost base, margin drops toward the FY2024 level (~41.5% adjusted) without reaching the 2023 trough, and recovers only to 46%.
bear.retention_note: Retention = 1.2 x revenue growth (one-for-one capital growth) PLUS 1.5% of revenue in FY2027-28 (~$400M/yr) to rebuild leverage capital as supplemental funding re-inflates the balance sheet; in FY2027 that nets to 1.5% because revenue is shrinking (capex 3.8 = 2.3 core + 1.5 rebuild). Terminal cap 12x FCFE for a de-rated rate-sensitive broker-bank.
bear.growth_note: FY2027 -6% (NII -12%, fees -3%, trading -5%), then 2-4.5% recovery on organic NNA that slows to ~4%.

base.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied adjusted pretax margin = EBITDA - SBC - D&A = [52.5, 52.5, 52.0, 51.5, 51.0, 51.0, ...]: holds the H1-2026 level through FY2028 as the last supplemental funding is repaid and sweep cash rebuilds, then gives back 150bps as Fed easing narrows the spread on new asset purchases and sweep-yield competition persists. 51% is ~1pp above FY2025's 50.0% and well above the 2023-24 trough (~38-42%).
base.growth_note: FY2027 +8%: core NNA ~5.5-6% plus modest market appreciation on fee assets and residual NIM recovery; fades to 3.5% by FY2036 as the NIM tailwind is exhausted and growth rests on organic asset gathering and pricing.
base.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 0.8 x revenue growth = [6.4, 5.6, 5.2, 4.8, 4.4, 4.0, 3.6, 3.6, 3.2, 2.8]% of revenue; at FY2027 that is ~$1.95B against ~$12.3B adjusted net income (84% payout), consistent with the 89-111% payouts of FY2025/H1-2026.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 10.0%/3.0% on FY2036 FCFE is ~14.7x, below the 16x cap, so Gordon binds. 14.7x FCFE is ~13.5x adjusted earnings - a de-rating from SCHW's ~20x 10-yr average P/E, which is deliberate for a mature, rate-sensitive franchise.

bull.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied adjusted pretax margin [54.0, 54.5, 55.0, 55.0, ...]: the Q2-2026 exit rate (53.9%) is the floor, not the peak - BDA balances keep returning to the balance sheet, lower-yielding legacy securities roll off into higher-yielding loans (record originations), and the post-integration cost base delivers operating leverage on record NNA.
bull.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 0.6 x revenue growth: AOCI pull-to-par (~$10.6B to recover) supplies part of the capital that balance-sheet growth would otherwise retain, and more of the growth is capital-light advice/managed-investing fees.
bull.growth_note: Core NNA holds at 6-7% (Q2-2026 annualised 5.8%, June a record), equity markets compound and managed-investing flows (+36% in 2025) lift the fee rate.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default, matching the treatment of NTRS. Bear held at 25% because the Analysis rates rate-path and cash-sorting risk as the two high-severity risks and the 2023 episode is three years old, not hypothetical; FY2026 earnings sit near peak NIM. Bull capped at 25% because it requires record NNA, further NIM expansion and benign markets simultaneously, and the stock already fell on a beat in Q2 - consensus targets (~$121) price much of it.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
